title: Prevention of Pollution of the Sea (Amendment) Bill
what_it_is: Prevention of Pollution of the Sea (Amendment) Bill

sections.label: Singapore acceding to Convention
sections.summary: Singapore will accede to the Convention as a responsible Flag State and Port State committed to marine environment protection and sustainable shipping.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: As a responsible Flag State and Port State committed to marine environment protection and sustainable shipping, Singapore will accede to the Convention.

sections.label: Revised fines and imprisonment
sections.summary: The revision increases the limit of fines from $10,000 to $20,000 and reduces the period of imprisonment from two years to six months.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: With the revision, the limit of fines is increased from $10,000 to $20,000, and the period of imprisonment is reduced from two years to six months.

sections.label: Ballast water discharge penalties aligned
sections.summary: Penalties for discharging untreated ballast water or sediments are aligned with revised penalties for discharging pollutants, garbage and noxious liquid substances into Singapore waters.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: The penalties for the discharge of untreated ballast water or sediments are aligned with the revised penalties for the discharge of pollutants, garbage and noxious liquid substances into our waters.

sections.label: Ballast water Convention background
sections.summary: Growing sea traffic led to invasive species from discharged ballast water causing ecological, economic and health issues, prompting the 2004 Convention requiring ballast water treatment before release.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: As the volume of sea traffic grew with the rise of international trade over the last 50 years, the environmental impact of the invasive species caused by the discharged ballast water has started to pose serious ecological, economic and health issues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This is the backdrop for the introduction of the International Convention for the Control and Management of Ships' Ballast Water and Sediments even back in 2004.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Under the Convention, ballast water will need to be treated before it is released into a new location so that any micro-organism or small marine species are eliminated before the ballast water is discharged into the open marine environment again.

sections.label: Convention worldwide force date
sections.summary: It will only come into force worldwide on 8 September 2017.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Yes, it will only come into force worldwide on 8 September 2017.

sections.label: Fines increased 100 percent
sections.summary: The $10,000 fine has been increased to $20,000, which is a 100% increase.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: At the moment, as I said just now, $10,000 has been increased to $20,000, and that is a 100% increase.

sections.label: Singapore and Ballast Water Convention
sections.summary: Singapore has been an early supporter of the Ballast Water Management Convention but ensures it can discharge obligations before acceding to any new convention.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: As the Member has noted, Singapore has also been an early supporter of the Ballast Water Management Convention.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: However, Singapore always ensures that we are able to discharge our obligations before acceding to any new convention.

sections.label: IMO revised guidelines completion
sections.summary: IMO revised its guidelines to make them more robust, a process completed in October 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: IMO, therefore, revised its guidelines to make them more robust.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: This process took some time and was only completed in October 2016, just last year.
